title: Etale local invariance at a point with algebraically closed residue field
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C$ be a locally finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $e:D\to C$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For $y\in D$ with $x=e(y)$, if either residue field $\kappa(x)$ or $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is isomorphic to $k$ as a $k$-algebra (that is, the field map $k\to\kappa(x)$, resp. $k\to\kappa(y)$, induced by the structure morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, resp. $D\to C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, is an isomorphism), then $x$ and $y$ are closed points [def-weil-closed-points], the induced residue-field map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ is an isomorphism, and the induced map on maximal-ideal-adic completed local rings $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,y}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is an isomorphism.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field) part (2): the residue extension kappa(y)/kappa(x) of an etale morphism is finite separable, hence trivial over kappa(x)=k algebraically closed; Morphisms Tag 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre) (2): a point with residue field algebraic over k is closed in a k-scheme; More on Algebra Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified), or Etale Morphisms Tag 039M (lemma-characterize-etale-completions) with the remark following it: the flat local map O_{C,x} -> O_{D,y} with m_x O_{D,y}=m_y and trivial residue extension induces an isomorphism of completions. This is the argument of the proof of Curves Tag 0C57.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{D,y}$ and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the actual stalk map of $e$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $e$ is flat and unramified; by [def-weil-unramified-morphism] it is locally of finite type. By [def-weil-flat-morphism], $\varphi$ is a flat local homomorphism. Thus neither flatness nor locality is being inferred from a merely abstract isomorphism of rings.

Apply implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-trf-unramified-maximal-ideal-residue-criterion] to $e$ at $y$, using the whole source $D$ as the unramified neighbourhood. Its locally-finite-type hypothesis holds by Step 1. It gives $\mathfrak m_A B=\mathfrak m_B$ for $\varphi$, and says that the actual induced map $\alpha:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ is a finite separable algebraic field extension.

Let $i:k\to\kappa(x)$ and $j:k\to\kappa(y)$ be the structural maps and $\alpha:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ the map from Step 2. The stalk-quotient construction of [def-weil-residue-field] gives $j=\alpha\circ i$. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-field-tower-rationality] with $K=\kappa(x)$ and $L=\kappa(y)$: $k$ is algebraically closed by hypothesis, $L/K$ is algebraic by Step 2, and the given disjunction concerns these very $i,j$. It makes $i,j,\alpha$ isomorphisms, so both residue extensions needed next have degree one.

source.place: Tags 09GQ (definition-algebraically-closed) and 09GR (lemma-algebraically-closed), triviality of algebraic extensions; the two-alternative tower argument is the expansion of old Step 3 of lem-trf-etale-completed-local-ring-iso.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-residue-tower-local-geometry] with $p:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the given structure morphism, $e:D\to C$ the given etale map, and the same $x=e(y)$. The two morphisms are locally of finite type by hypothesis and Step 1. The required residue maps are $i$ and $\alpha$, both degree-one extensions by Step 3. The lemma gives ambient closedness of $x,y$ and makes the actual stalks $A,B$ Noetherian local rings; its germ-localization presentations identify precisely these stalks. This uses no global quasi-compactness.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre), closedness in the fibre and ascent over a closed base point; Morphisms Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), twice. For the affine-local presentations: Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), clause (6), and Algebra Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), localization clause. This isolates old Steps 4--6 of lem-trf-etale-completed-local-ring-iso.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-completion-iso] to the actual map $\varphi:A\to B$. Its hypotheses are verified separately: Noetherian local rings by Step 4, flatness and locality by Step 1, $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ by Step 2, and an isomorphism on residue fields by Step 3. Its conclusion is that $\varphi^\wedge:A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is an isomorphism. The cited statement specifies this very map on compatible residue classes by $(a_n\bmod\mathfrak m_A^n)_n\mapsto(\varphi(a_n)\bmod\mathfrak m_B^n)_n$, so it is exactly the induced completed-local-ring map in the item. Together with Steps 3--4 this proves all the required clauses.

lean.statement: theorem etale_completedLocalRing_iso {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C D : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (e : D ⟶ C) [Etale e] (y : D) (hres : Function.Bijective (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ C.Γevaluation (e y)).hom) ∨ Function.Bijective (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ (e ≫ f).appTop ≫ D.Γevaluation y).hom)) : e y ∈ closedPoints C ∧ y ∈ closedPoints D ∧ IsIso (e.residueFieldMap y) ∧ ∃ (ehat : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk (e y))) (C.presheaf.stalk (e y)) →+* AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (D.presheaf.stalk y)) (D.presheaf.stalk y)), (∀ (n : ℕ) (z : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk (e y))) (C.presheaf.stalk (e y))) (a : C.presheaf.stalk (e y)), AdicCompletion.evalₐ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk (e y))) n z = Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk (e y)) ^ n) a → AdicCompletion.evalₐ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (D.presheaf.stalk y)) n (ehat z) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (D.presheaf.stalk y) ^ n) ((e.stalkMap y).hom a)) ∧ Function.Bijective ehat
